As above, denote by r3(N) the largest size of a subset of [1; N], free of three-term arithmetic progressions. Using results of [77] (see previous problem), Stanchescu showed in [88] that j2Aj 0:5n(n=r3(n))1=4, and on the other hand, that there there are arbitrarily large n 2 N and corresponding n-element sets A Z Z, free of collinear triples, such that j2Aj n exp(C p lnn) (with an absolute constant C).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}$, let $2A := A+A = \{a+b : a,b\in A\}$ denote its sumset, and let $r_3(N)$ denote the largest size of a subset of $\{1,2,\dots,N\}$ containing no three-term arithmetic progression.

Define
$$ f(n) := \min\{\,|2A| : A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z},\ |A|=n,\ \text{no three points of } A \text{ are collinear}\,\}. $$

It is known that
$$ f(n) \ge \tfrac{1}{2}\, n\, \bigl(n/r_3(n)\bigr)^{1/4}, $$
and that there exist arbitrarily large $n$ and corresponding $n$-element collinear-triple-free sets $A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}$ with
$$ |2A| \le n\,\exp\!\bigl(C\sqrt{\ln n}\bigr) $$
for some absolute constant $C>0$.

Determine the true order of magnitude of $f(n)$ as $n\to\infty$. In particular, close the gap between the above lower and upper bounds.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem attributed to G. Freiman, with the best known bounds being Stanchescu's lower bound $|2A|\ge 0.5 n(n/r_3(n))^{1/4}$ and an upper bound $n\exp(C\sqrt{\ln n})$. No subsequent work resolving the gap was located.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Additive Combinatorics
status_evidence.snippet: Stanchescu showed that |2A| >= 0.5 n (n/r_3(n))^{1/4}, and there are arbitrarily large n with collinear-triple-free A such that |2A| <= n exp(C sqrt(ln n)).
status_evidence.claim: Best known bounds; gap remains open.
